entityDescription:
IOER Leitbild 
The Leibniz Institute of Ecological Urban and Regional Development (IOER) is a non-university research centre and a member of the Leibniz Association. With the present vision and mission statement (Leitbild) we formulate strategic directions for the future development of the IOER. The Leitbild provides long-term orientations for our research and transfer activities, which are further operationalised in our research programme. It equally stipulates principles in terms of organisation, management and cooperation. The Leitbild was developed in an open co-creation process with the staff members and is updated regularly.
Our research subject
Current scientific evidence underlines the urgent need for socio-ecological transformations in spatial terms in order to achieve fundamental sustainability goals. Human activity exerts spatially differentiated pressures on the Earth system at all scales. Processes of industrialization and demographic change drive excessive local or telecoupled environmental pressures, with major regional variation in growth dynamics. This includes ecosystem destruction, species extinction, resource extraction, pollutant emissions, soil sealing or waste disposal, among others. In turn human settlements are increasingly exposed to diverse natural hazards with highly uneven geographical distributions. In this, technologies and especially digitalization play an ambivalent role since they can both reinforce and alleviate pressures and risks.
In view of these challenges we investigate the features, patterns and dynamics of socio-ecological-technological spatial configurations. Our research focuses on landscapes, the built environment, land use and economic interactions to explore and compare their development and transformation, particularly in the territorial context of urban districts, cities and agglomerations, urbanized and rural areas, as well as regions and countries - including cross-border areas. Key environmental factors we examine are the regional climate, ecosystems, biodiversity, resources and natural hazards. As corresponding physical factors of society we study technologies, materials and energy. Ultimately, our principal concern is the spatial coevolution of these factors with societal institutions, cultures and practices regarding sustainability and resilience impacts. This implies especially considering the role of different individuals and actors, their intersectionality and interactions, as well as society as a whole in co-shaping spatial developments.

entityDescription:
Transform Transport is a non-profit research foundation based in Milan (Italy) and focused on innovation in mobility and transport planning. It provides innovative, inclusive, and sustainable mobility solutions for shaping the future of society and cities worldwide in line with the UN’s SDG 11 (Sustainable cities and communities).
 
It grounds on 30 years of Systematica’s work and explores how disruptive technologies, increasingly and rapidly influencing urban mobility, can have a positive impact on cities, neighborhoods, and buildings, collaborating closely with municipalities and companies, and using Big Data for greater insights.
 
Transform Transport actively participates in lectures, talks, and hackathons in partnership with Universities, mentoring and sharing methodologies with students. It also promotes and develops research studies, disseminating them through books, publications, conferences, public talks, and events.
 
Our focus is from one side on researches and on the presentation of proposals at Italian and International levels.
 
Regarding the main strategic themes on which TT aims the research, the topics are the following:
 
1. Urban Mobility Metrics (as e.g. Wi-fi data, Carsharing data and Walklability for children)
2. Livable Street (as e.g. Milan Sidewalks Map and 15-minute City Model)
 
With reference to the proposals submitted, STEP UP – Walkability for women in Milan has been awarded by Fondazione Cariplo and it focuses on the needs and expectations of women while walking.
Transform Transport is coordinating the project for 12 months in collaboration withTeMA Lab– Università degli Studi di Napoli Federico II,Sex and the City, andWalk21 Foundation.
The project results will help identify challenging areas or neighborhoods in the city of Milan, which can serve as the analytical testbed to develop a set of policy recommendations aimed at enhancing the level of walkability for women in cities. In particular, the collected disaggregated data will be used to support the definition of guidelines and policies for the design of future transport services, focusing on the impact of individual characteristics of pedestrians in relation to their gender on the perceived level of walkability. In the event of the identification of distinct problematic areas or zones, the project outcome will also highlight potential physical interventions via tactical urbanism approaches in public spaces.

Skypuzzler is a pioneering company, revolutionising the aviation industry by offering a breakthrough solution for managing drone air traffic. Our team comprises of experienced air traffic controllers and computer scientists, supported by a professional board of directors with decades of business and technical knowledge.

Imagine a puzzle in the sky, where drones need to navigate through a complex network of airspace without colliding with each other or other objects. Skypuzzler has developed advanced software that works as a Digital Air Traffic Control system specifically designed to manage drones as a module integrated into the existing digital infrastructure (Unmanned traffic Management systems). This technology allows drones to fly safely and autonomously by providing clear paths and instructions. One of the most exciting aspects of our solution is the concept of "Free Route Airspace” for drones, enabling efficient and safe flight paths, while also fostering drone business growth.

As the drone industry grows unprecedentedly, efficient and safe airspace management becomes more critical than ever. A robust Digital Air Traffic Control system is essential to harness the full potential of drones across various sectors, such as logistics, agriculture, surveillance, and even public services. This technology is the key to scaling the drone industry, ensuring seamless operations, collision avoidance, and regulation compliance. In addition, our solution indirectly contributes to the global goal of reducing CO2 emissions by making drones a preferred choice for last-mile deliveries, thus reducing the environmental impact of transportation.

Cosmodity SRL is an innovative deep-tech startup developing a conceptually new technology and service, called muLINER, for long-term Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) exploiting the natural phenomenon of highly-penetrating Cosmic Rays as a stable straight-line reference.
This technology combines proprietary hardware and software with complex reconstruction algorithms to directly measure mm-level displacements at multiple points of a structure that are tens of metres apart, while maintaining this accuracy constant throughout many years.
These aspects make muLINER particularly suitable for monitoring large multi-storey buildings, bridges, viaducts, underground tunnels, etc.
 
The know-how comes from extensive research at the intersection of fundamental high-energy physics and detector R&D for hadron-therapy applications.
The commercialisation of this technology has been supported by a Technology Transfer grant from the Italian Institute of Nuclear Physics (INFN Torino) to reach TRL5, while further R&D is expected to bring this technology to TRL9 with the financial and technical support from ESA.

entityName: Luka Koper, port and logistic system, public limited company
entityDescription:
The Port of Koper is Slovenia’s only multipurpose seaport and a strategically important logistics hub for hinterland markets. Located at the northernmost point of the Adriatic Sea, the port integrates maritime, rail, and road transport services, enabling efficient cargo handling and transport operations. Owing to its favourable geographic position and strong hinterland connections, the Port of Koper serves as one of the main maritime gateways for markets of Central and Southeastern Europe. Through its economic activity, the port significantly shapes the urban and economic development of Koper and the wider Slovenian coastal region. At the same time, it plays a vital role in strengthening Slovenia’s international trade competitiveness and logistics connectivity within the European TEN-T transport network. The port is particularly recognised as an important container and automotive hub in the Adriatic region, with a strong dependence on sustainable rail transport, as more than 50% of cargo is transported by rail. 
In 2008, Luka Koper d.d. entered into a concession agreement with the Republic of Slovenia for the provision of port services, as well as for the management, development, and regular maintenance of port infrastructure within the Koper cargo port area. In accordance with the Slovenian Maritime Code, the concession was granted for a period of 35 years and covers the entire concession area of the Port of Koper.
Luka Koper d.d. operates all 12 specialised terminals within the port, each tailored to specific cargo categories and equipped with modern handling equipment and advanced port technology. Through these terminals, Luka Koper d.d. provides cargo handling, transhipment, warehousing, and value-added logistics services, ensuring comprehensive support across the supply chain. In addition to its commercial activities, Luka Koper d.d. performs two mandatory public utility services: the regular maintenance of port infrastructure intended for public transport and the collection of ship-generated waste within the port area. The company is also responsible for managing the port’s economic zone and for the continuous development of port infrastructure and suprastructure, supporting the port’s long-term competitiveness and sustainable growth.
